title: Risk-classified contract intake and auto-routing for Dedicated & Private deals
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
We need an automated intake and routing system that classifies incoming enterprise contract redlines (MSA/DPA/SLAs) by risk vector (indemnity cap, liability carve-outs, data residency, encryption/KMS, export controls) and routes them to the minimal necessary review path: self-serve AM approval, product-managed concessions, legal redline review, or cross-functional incident response (security/compliance). The goal is to reduce manual triage time for high-volume mid-market deals, accelerate turnaround for low-risk concessions, and provide deterministic pricing/packaging adjustments for common liability exceptions.

Why now:
- Increasing volume of Dedicated & Private deals is creating a backlog for legal and SE teams.
- We observed 20% longer sales cycles on deals requesting indemnity/escrow changes in Q4.
- Pricing experiments show predictable uplift when low-risk concessions are auto-approved with a standardized discount.

Goals and success metrics:
- Median time-to-first-response for contract intake reduces from 3 business days to <8 business hours for low-risk submissions.
- >60% of incoming redlines are auto-classified; >30% are auto-routed to non-legal paths with SLAs.
- Revenue capture: convert 15% of at-risk deals to closed-won by offering packaged concessions with explicit pricing offsets.
- Auditability: every automated decision must be logged with evidence (scoring, rule trigger, reviewer override).

Scope and what we will build:
1) Risk taxonomy: formalize risk categories and mapping to pricing/approval levels (Low/Medium/High).
2) Intake form overhaul: add structured fields for indemnity cap, liability carve-outs, data residency, escrow requests, and SSO/SAML constraints.
3) Scoring engine (config-driven rules + ML signals): deterministic rules for common flags (e.g., indemnity > $X => High), plus a lightweight ML model to detect unusual clause language.
4) Auto-routing engine: integrate with Linear/GH/Confluence and route to the correct queue (Sales Ops, Legal async review, Security) and optionally surface a templated concession package with price delta for the AM.
5) UI & Console: a contract intake dashboard for AMs with decision rationale, manual override, and one-click “approve with pricing” action.
6) Telemetry and rollback: metrics for override rates, false positives/negatives, and a safe path for immediate escalation to legal.

Acceptance criteria:
- Taxonomy and rulebook documented in Confluence and signed off by Legal and Security.
- Prototype scoring engine correctly classifies 90% of a 200-sample backlog set (manual label).
- Integration tests to route dummy submissions to queues; logs include rule triggers and a trace ID.
- AM-facing UI mockup validated with 3 pilot AE/SEs and incorporated feedback.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Full ML-based clause parsing beyond lightweight anomaly detection.
- Contract negotiations and redline edits (legal team retains edit authority).

Trade-offs considered:
- Deterministic rules are faster to ship but require continuous tuning. We will adopt a hybrid approach (rules + model) with rules first.
- Automated concessions reduce friction but increase pricing leakage risk; therefore we will limit auto-approve to low-risk tags and require pricing offsets.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (Docs & Rulebook): 2 weeks — agree taxonomy and map to existing legal SLAs.
- Phase 1 (Intake + Basic Rules): 3 weeks — deploy form and deterministic routing for low/medium risk. Pilot with 2 AE teams.
- Phase 2 (Pricing Pack & UI): 2 weeks — enable templated concessions and AM approval flow.
- Phase 3 (ML & Expand): 3–4 weeks — integrate ML signal and expand to more regions.

Monitoring & telemetry:
- Dashboard: intake volume, classification distribution, time-to-first-response, override rate, revenue impact estimate.
- Alerts: surge in high-risk submissions or override rate >25% for >3 days.

Risks & mitigation:
- False negatives (high-risk routed incorrectly): hard stop — all high severity flags default to legal review.
- Sales pushback on process rigidity: provide manual override and clear SLAs so AMs can move quickly.
- Pricing leakage: require a pricing offset and record approvals in CRM; limit auto-approve to template-based concessions.

Next steps & asks:
- Legal: review taxonomy and threshold definitions (indemnity caps, escrow triggers).
- Security/Compliance: confirm data residency and KMS-related flags to be surfaced.
- Engineering: estimate integration work for queues and logs (ENG-31211 listed as dependency).
- Design: three mockups for AM dashboard and intake UX (link in attachments).
comments: 2025-02-14 — Aisha Patel: Created ticket after workshop with Sales and Legal. Captured initial pain points and metrics. Attached backlog samples for classifier training.

2025-02-18 — Legal (Priya Shah): Reviewed taxonomy draft; requested explicit handling for escrow and export control clauses. Suggested threshold values for indemnity tiers. See Confluence notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EC/Taxonomy+v1
2025-02-20 — Marco Ruiz: Spoke with two pilot AE leaders. They want the AM dashboard to show the suggested pricing delta and a one-click accept. Added as acceptance criteria.

2025-02-25 — Eng (Samir Khan): Quick feasibility: basic deterministic routing is low effort; ML model will need labeled dataset (we have ~1.2k historical deals). Created ENG-31211 to own intake infra work.
2025-03-03 — Design (Elena Gomez): Uploaded 3 mockups in Figma and iterated based on pilot AE feedback. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/contract-intake-ui
2025-03-03 — Aisha Patel: Updated estimates after sync with Legal and Eng. Moving to Planned and assigning Marco as PM lead for pilot coordination.
